title: Wynona’s diary years
status: editorial prototype; claims and rights await Beth’s review
opening: In 1879, an eleven-year-old in the Drumore circle began collecting words from relatives and friends. Eleven years later, Jessie Wynona Lamborn began a diary. Its pages move between school, worship, travel, weather, friendship and loss. This story follows five moments in that surviving account, with the archive trail beside each one.
ending: The diary continues beyond these five moments. Here, Wynona’s own words and the family archive offer a route through a particular year, not a complete account of her life. Beth’s review of the diary, identities, captions and permissions is the next editorial step.
